title: bug: cutover real-root acceptance exceeds the 10000-entry manifest bound
description:
Found while verifying parent task-78eedd8ebc2b43c581ac21ea28648a9a: pnpm test at a7dc26999a1fe92edee501953206a6ae54377038 + four UI/docs reopen diffs exits 1 solely at tests/migration/cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts:536 (assertOk :73): CUTOVER_MANIFEST_ENTRY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED @ cutover-manifest, entry count exceeds 10000.
The same path/code is recorded in parent comment-3b5de9a4 before reopen; current evidence comment-660e46b8. Real-root acceptance includes generated/runtime material and exceeds the bounded capture. Re-measure the admitted population and intended exclusions; do not simply weaken the limit or clean foreign files. No active matching cutover/manifest/10000 task found in list_tasks.
definitionOfDone: Reproduce the exact CUTOVER_MANIFEST_ENTRY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED at the real-root acceptance and identify which admitted path populations exceed the bound without exposing credentials.
Implement the approved bounded capture or acceptance-scope correction with red-first regression coverage; preserve necessary cutover coverage, fail-closed limits, and peer/generated files.
Fresh focused cutover gate passes with nonzero tests; disclose full root result and path-attributed foreign failures.

implementationPlan.description:
REPRODUCE THE EXACT REFUSAL AND NAME THE POPULATION THAT CAUSED IT (DoD 1). NO EDITS.

Run the focused lane FOREGROUND and STANDALONE — no pipe, no `;`-chain, since a piped run reports tail's exit code: `pnpm test:migration`. Confirm it exits 1 at tests/migration/cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts:536 with `CUTOVER_MANIFEST_ENTRY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED @ cutover-manifest`, and quote the count line and exit code verbatim.

THEN MEASURE THE ADMITTED POPULATION, which is the actual deliverable of this step. Mirror the walk's four current exclusions exactly (`.git`, `dist`, `node_modules`, `target` — cutover-manifest.ts:119-124):
  find . \( -name node_modules -o -name .git -o -name dist -o -name target \) -prune -o -print | wc -l
  ... | awk -F/ '{print ($2==""?"<root>":$2)}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
At plan time this answered 10568 total, led by `.serena` 4302, apps 2884, packages 1763, `.moe` 1101. RE-MEASURE rather than trusting those numbers — `.serena` grows by one file per agent session, so it will have moved.

ESTABLISH THE DECISIVE FACT, the one that turns this from "the repo got big" into a scope defect: run `git check-ignore -v` on one file under `.serena/memories/`. At plan time it answered `C:/Users/Yaron/.gitignore_global:1:.serena/` — ignored by a HOST-GLOBAL gitignore that lives OUTSIDE the repository. That means the acceptance walk's population is a property of this MACHINE, not of the tree, and the arm can never be stable. Record the check-ignore output verbatim.

NO CREDENTIALS: report directory names and counts only. Do not paste file contents or memory bodies, and do not paste the global ignore file wholesale — the one matching line is the evidence.

Record all four results in the step note. If `.serena` is NOT the dominant population on your run, STOP and report what is — the rest of this plan is aimed at the population step 1 actually measures.

implementationPlan.description:
RED FIRST, AND MAKE THE ARM PROVE THE EXCLUSION RATHER THAN THE BOUND (DoD 2).

Add one arm to tests/migration/cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts. It must go RED before step 3's production change and GREEN after — write it and watch it fail before touching cutover-manifest.ts.

WHAT IT MUST NOT BE: a second copy of the existing bound arm at :335, which already drives `captureCutoverManifest(root, { maxEntries: 3 })` into `CUTOVER_MANIFEST_ENTRY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`. Re-proving the refusal branch adds nothing. And it must NOT depend on the host's real `.serena` population: that directory is ignored by a gitignore outside the repository, so on a clean CI host or fresh clone it may be small or absent, and an arm anchored on it would be red here and green there — worse than no arm.

WHAT IT MUST BE: over a CONSTRUCTED fixture (use the existing `fixture()` helper at :68), create a directory whose name is the one step 3 adds to the defaults, put enough files under it to matter, and assert BOTH halves of the exclusion contract the file header promises:
  (a) the walk did NOT descend it — no manifest entry has a path under that directory; and
  (b) it IS DECLARED — the name appears in `manifest.excludedDirectories`, because the header's guarantee is that "a walk that skipped more than it admits cannot masquerade as a match". An exclusion that is silently applied is the defect this arm exists to prevent.
Assert the DECLARATION, not merely the absence: absence alone is also what a broken walk that returned nothing produces.

Also add the negative that keeps the default meaningful: pass `excludedDirectoryNames: []` and confirm the same tree DOES yield entries under that directory. Without it, an arm asserting only absence stays green if the walk breaks entirely.

Run the single file and quote the failing assertion. A red-first arm that was never seen red is not red-first.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 2 — RED-FIRST ARM ADDED AND SEEN RED. Production file NOT touched (`git diff --stat` shows the test file only, 48 insertions, cutover-manifest.ts absent).

ADDED: `TASK-MF ARM C3: the host-local agent memory store is excluded by DEFAULT and DECLARED` at tests/migration/cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts:490-537, inside the existing TASK-MF describe, immediately after ARM C2 and before `manifestOf`.

WHAT IT DRIVES: the existing `fixture()` helper at :63 (a real mkdtemp tree, torn down by the registered cleanup), plus `mkdirSync`/`writeFileSync`/`join` already imported at :19-21. It creates `<root>/.serena/memories/` with 12 real files and runs `captureCutoverManifest(root)` through the REAL default node ports — no port fake, so the production walk is what is under test.

BOTH HALVES OF THE EXCLUSION CONTRACT, IN ONE ASSERTION. I first wrote them as two sequential expects and the run stopped at (a), leaving (b) never seen red — a half-witnessed red-first. Rewrote as a single object comparison so one failure reports both:
  expect({ descended: entries.some(p => p.startsWith(".serena/")), declared: excludedDirectories.includes(".serena") }).toEqual({ descended: false, declared: true })
Asserting the DECLARATION and not merely the absence is the point: absence alone is also what a walk that returned nothing produces, and `CUTOVER_MANIFEST_EXCLUSION_MISMATCH` can only fail closed on a widened exclusion if the widening is on the record.

THE NEGATIVE that keeps the default meaningful: a second capture with `excludedDirectoryNames: []` over the SAME tree asserts the 12 `.serena/**` entries DO appear, `excludedDirectories` is `[]`, and `admitted.entryCount === excluded.entryCount + 12`. Without it an absence-only arm would stay green if the walk broke entirely.

HOST-INDEPENDENT BY CONSTRUCTION: it never reads the host's real `.serena`. That directory is ignored by a gitignore outside the repo (step 1), so on a fresh clone or CI host it is absent or tiny; an arm anchored on it would be red here and green there. This one asserts the same thing on any host.

RED WITNESSED, verbatim, `npx vitest run --config tests/migration/vitest.config.ts cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts -t "ARM C3"` EXIT 1:
`Test Files  1 failed (1)` / `Tests  1 failed | 24 skipped (25)`
`AssertionError: expected { descended: true, declared: false } to deeply equal { descended: false, declared: true }`
` at cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts:524:8`
That is exactly the defect: today the walk DOES descend the store and does NOT declare it.

FILE SIZE: cutover-drill.test.ts goes 579 -> 622 lines. It was already over 400 at HEAD before this row; the plan mandates adding the arm here (it is the file that owns every other TASK-MF arm and the acceptance it repairs), so no split was in scope for this row. Flagging it rather than silently absorbing it.

FOREIGN DIRT unchanged and untouched: `.moe/**`, `.codex/*`, `.grok/config.toml`, docs/agent-stack-runbook.md, apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/activity-screens.{tsx,test.tsx}, apps/daemon/src/http/affordance-read.ts, tests/e2e/control-room/deploy-migrations.spec.ts, and the untracked peer files.

implementationPlan.description:
THE SCOPE CORRECTION — EXCLUDE HOST-LOCAL AGENT STATE, AND DO NOT TOUCH THE BOUND (DoD 2).

In tests/migration/cutover/cutover-manifest.ts, add `.serena` to `DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_NAMES` (:119-124), keeping the list sorted as it is now.

WHY THIS IS THE PRINCIPLED FIX AND NOT A DODGE, and say so in the code: the file header already states the exclusion criterion — `node_modules` is excluded because it is a tree "that no cutover is about", and every excluded name is "DEPENDENCY OR DERIVED OUTPUT, never source". `.serena` is an agent memory store ignored by a gitignore OUTSIDE this repository; its size is a property of the developer's machine, not of the tree being cut over. It is the same category as `node_modules`, arrived at from the other direction.

DO NOT CHANGE `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES`. The DoD forbids weakening the limit, and cutover-drill.test.ts:339 pins it at exactly 10_000 — a change there would correctly go red. The bound is not the defect; the admitted population was.

UPDATE THE STALE MEASUREMENT COMMENT at :112-117 rather than deleting it. It currently reads "MEASURED 2026-09-03 on this checkout: 22473 non-node_modules files ... falling to 8257 with these four excluded, which is what fits under MAX_WALK_ENTRIES without moving that bound." That is five days old and the tree measured 10568 at plan time. Rewrite it with YOUR measured numbers from step 1, DATE it, and — this is the part worth writing down — record that the earlier figure was calibrated against a quantity that moves, which is why the bound re-armed. A comment that just carries a fresher number teaches the next reader nothing.

DO NOT ALSO EXCLUDE `.moe` IN THIS STEP. It is roughly 1100 entries of which ~1034 are TRACKED repository content, and whether a cutover is "about" the Moe board store is a scope question nobody has measured. Excluding it would make 1034 tracked files' movement invisible to a manifest whose stated job is proving bytes did not move. With `.serena` excluded the walk sits near 6266 against a 10000 bound — ample headroom — so this does not need deciding now. If your step 1 measurement shows `.moe` alone would breach the bound, STOP and escalate with the numbers instead of folding it in.

Now re-run step 2's arm and confirm it goes GREEN.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 3 — SCOPE CORRECTION LANDED. `.serena` added to DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_NAMES; the BOUND IS UNTOUCHED.

THE CHANGE (tests/migration/cutover/cutover-manifest.ts):
- `DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_NAMES` is now `[".git", ".serena", "dist", "node_modules", "target"]`. Sorted as before — `.git` < `.serena` by the same UTF-8 byte order the walk itself sorts `excludedDirectories` with (`g` 0x67 < `s` 0x73), and both dot-names still precede `dist` (`.` 0x2E < `d` 0x64).
- `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES` UNCHANGED: `grep -n "MAX_WALK_ENTRIES = "` => `95:export const MAX_WALK_ENTRIES = 10_000;`. cutover-drill.test.ts:339 pins that literal and stayed green, which is the check that a weakened limit would have tripped.
- No other production symbol touched. No new seam: `CutoverWalkOptions.excludedDirectoryNames` already existed, which is why the red-first arm needed no production affordance of its own.

THE COMMENT REWRITE (:109-138), which is the part with a shelf life. The old block said "MEASURED 2026-09-03 ... 22473 non-node_modules files ... falling to 8257 with these four excluded, which is what fits under MAX_WALK_ENTRIES without moving that bound." I did not just refresh the number. The rewrite records WHY the bound re-armed: 8257 was calibrated against a quantity that GROWS ON ITS OWN — `.serena` gains a file per agent session — so the headroom was being spent by sessions rather than by the repository, and five days later the same walk measured 10574 and refused. It states the criterion the list already implied and now widens by one category ("DEPENDENCY, DERIVED OUTPUT OR HOST-LOCAL TOOL STATE — never source, and never something a cutover is about"), carries my step 1 numbers DATED 2026-09-08 with the exact `find` command inline, and names the check-ignore evidence generically as `<home>/.gitignore_global:1:.serena/` rather than pasting a host path.
It also records, in the code, why `.moe` is deliberately NOT excluded: 1101 entries of which 1034 are TRACKED repository content, and hiding tracked files from a manifest whose job is proving bytes did not move is the opposite of this list's criterion.

ESCALATION CONDITION DID NOT FIRE. Step 3 says stop if `.moe` alone would breach the bound. It is 1101 against 10_000 — nowhere near — so `.moe` stays admitted and undecided, as planned.

MEASURED EFFECT: 10574 admitted with the four original exclusions, 6271 with `.serena` also pruned — 37% under the unchanged 10_000.

GREEN CONFIRMED:
- step 2's arm, `npx vitest run --config tests/migration/vitest.config.ts cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts -t "ARM C3"` EXIT 0, `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  1 passed | 24 skipped (25)`. Same arm was EXIT 1 with `{descended: true, declared: false}` before this edit.
- whole drill file, EXIT 0, `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  25 passed (25)`, 11.67s. That includes ARM E against the REAL repo root — the acceptance this row was filed on now passes, from the population side, with the limit intact.

File is 387 lines (was 365); under the 400 split threshold. Foreign dirty paths untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
STOP THE BOUND FROM RE-ARMING SILENTLY (DoD 2). This is the step that decides whether the next agent to hit this pays the same attribution cost this row just paid.

The failure that opened this row was a bare `CUTOVER_MANIFEST_ENTRY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED @ cutover-manifest, entry count exceeds 10000` at ARM E. It names the LIMIT but not the POPULATION, so whoever hits it next has to rediscover, as this row did, that 41% of the walk was one host-local directory. Fix the diagnostic, not the number.

In ARM E (cutover-drill.test.ts:532-545), when `captureCutoverManifest(REPO_ROOT)` refuses, fail with a message that names the top-level populations — the counts per first path segment, largest first — and the declared `excludedDirectories`. Build it from what the walk ALREADY produced or from a cheap directory count; do NOT run a second full walk inside a case that already hashes thousands of files under a 300_000 ms budget.

Also assert the headroom POSITIVELY on the success path, so the arm reports the margin rather than only the breach: after `assertOk`, assert `entryCount` is under `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES` and record the measured margin in the failure text. Do NOT freeze a count literal — `expect(entryCount).toBe(6266)` would be a number the next peer commit moves, and this epic's rails forbid frozen roster counts for exactly that reason. Assert the RELATION to the bound, never the value.

Keep every existing ARM E assertion exactly as written: `entryCount > 0`, entries length equals entryCount, `excludedDirectories.length > 0`, and `excludedDirectories` contains `node_modules`. Add to them; weaken nothing.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 4 — ARM E NOW NAMES THE POPULATION, NOT JUST THE LIMIT. Only tests/migration/cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts touched.

THE DIAGNOSTIC. `assertOk(result)` in ARM E is replaced by an explicit `if (!result.ok)` branch that throws a message carrying, in order: the code, layer, detail and stop path; the ADMITTED POPULATION by top-level segment, largest first; the EXCLUSIONS IN FORCE; and the instruction that a segment which is host-local tool state belongs in DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_NAMES, because raising the bound against a population that grows on its own only defers the failure. Same assertion (ok:true or fail) — nothing weakened, the generic JSON dump replaced by the facts a reader has to act on. TypeScript narrows on the discriminated union exactly as `assertOk` did (`npx tsc -p tests/migration/tsconfig.json --noEmit` EXIT 0).

THE CENSUS HELPER `countByTopSegment` (added above ARM E). Counts dirents only — it NEVER opens or hashes a file, so it costs what `find` costs, not what the manifest walk costs — and it runs ONLY inside the failure branch, in a case that has already failed. No second hashing walk inside the 300_000 ms budget, per the plan and risk 4. It mirrors DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_NAMES so the counts describe the ADMITTED population (the number that must come down), does not follow symlinks, swallows an unreadable directory rather than letting the diagnostic itself become the failure, and caps output at the 12 largest segments.

HEADROOM ASSERTED POSITIVELY, VALUE NOT FROZEN. After the four existing expects: `expect(entryCount, "walked N entries under MAX_WALK_ENTRIES=10000, margin M").toBeLessThan(MAX_WALK_ENTRIES)`. The RELATION to the bound, never the literal — `toBe(6271)` is a number the next peer commit moves, and this epic's rails forbid frozen counts. I am being straight about its strength: since the walk refuses at the bound, the ok path can only reach exactly MAX_WALK_ENTRIES, so this assertion's main work is printing the margin. That is why I did not stop there.

THE ASSERTION THAT DOES CARRY WEIGHT — bidirectional, and host-independent. `readdirSync(REPO_ROOT)` (one readdir of the root, not a walk) collects the default-excluded names that ACTUALLY EXIST as top-level directories on this tree, asserts that set is NON-EMPTY (a sweep yielding zero cases would otherwise pass), then asserts each one is DECLARED in `manifest.excludedDirectories`. Derived from the real tree rather than from a fixed list, so it holds on a clean host where `.serena` is absent, and it catches the failure a `toContain("node_modules")` subset check cannot: a name configured in the defaults that the walk never applies. On this checkout it covers `.git`, `.serena` and `node_modules`.

EXISTING ASSERTIONS KEPT VERBATIM, ADDED TO ONLY: `entryCount > 0`, `entries` length equals `entryCount`, `excludedDirectories.length > 0`, `excludedDirectories` contains `node_modules` — all four unchanged and still in their original order.

IMPORTS: `readdirSync` and `type { Dirent }` from node:fs; `DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_NAMES` added to the existing cutover-manifest.js import. No `any`.

GREEN: `npx vitest run --config tests/migration/vitest.config.ts cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts` EXIT 0, `Test Files  1 passed (1)` / `Tests  25 passed (25)`, 10.92s.

NOT YET PROVEN, and step 5 is where it gets proven: the refusal branch has not yet been SEEN to render. Step 5's drill (removing `.serena` from the defaults) reds ARM E on this host, which is exactly the input that exercises it — I will quote the rendered census verbatim there rather than claim the branch works because it compiles.

File is 705 lines, up from 622. Already over the 400 threshold at HEAD before this row; the plan places both the arm and the diagnostic in this file, so no split was in scope. Flagged, not absorbed silently. Foreign dirty paths untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
ONE CONCENTRATED VERIFICATION PASS: DRILL, GATES, ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (DoD 3).

THE DRILL, because a scope-correction arm is exactly the kind that can pass vacuously: remove `.serena` from `DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_DIRECTORY_NAMES` and confirm BOTH step 2's exclusion arm and (on this host) ARM E go RED, naming the missing exclusion. Then restore. Both mutated paths are TRACKED, so prove the restore with an EMPTY `git diff -- tests/migration/cutover/cutover-manifest.ts tests/migration/cutover/cutover-drill.test.ts`, run in a call SEPARATE from the restore itself. `git status --porcelain` those two paths BEFORE you start.

GATES, each FOREGROUND and STANDALONE, exit code AND count line quoted verbatim:
- `pnpm test:migration` — the focused lane, and DoD 3 requires a NONZERO test count. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code: "No test files found" and "0 passed" are both exit 0, and the discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` line, which a vacuous run never prints.
- `pnpm test` — the full root result DoD 3 asks you to disclose. It is the ROOT lane only (its vitest include has no `apps/**`), which is fine here because `tests/migration` is in it — but never quote its count as evidence about an apps/** package.
- `pnpm typecheck`.

PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE (global rail 3), and it matters on this row because the checkout is dirty with seven foreign paths: record repo-wide failures at the merge-base and at HEAD, and complete only when the delta intersected with this row's two owned files is EMPTY. Disclose any foreign red VERBATIM with its exact failing lines and file paths — do not fix it, do not revert peer dirt, and do not call it green.

ADVERSARIAL PASS (load `adversarial-self-review`). Ask specifically: on a CLEAN CI host where `.serena` is absent or holds only its tracked files, does step 2's arm still prove something? It must — it drives a constructed fixture, not the host's real tree. And: could the new exclusion hide a real cutover difference? Answer it against the header's own contract — the excluded name is DECLARED in `excludedDirectories`, and `CUTOVER_MANIFEST_EXCLUSION_MISMATCH` refuses any comparison whose two captures declared different sets, so a hidden difference cannot masquerade as a match.
implementationPlan.note:
STEP 5 — DRILL, GATES, ADVERSARIAL PASS. All green. Full detail of the adversarial finding is in comment-e5d1692b.

THE DRILL — PROCESS-LOCAL, so the shared checkout was NEVER written. `browser-e2e-gate` was held by worker-bcaa6d5e/task-817d893f throughout, and the standing rule is that a drill on a tracked shared file under ANY live lease must be process-local. I used the out-of-tree vitest transform recipe: `%TEMP%/moe-8933-drill-worker-812079a7/vitest.drill.mjs`, zero imports, plain object literal, a `enforce:"pre"` plugin that drops `".serena",` from the source at transform time and SELF-PROVES it fired (`throw` unless the anchor matches exactly 1 site).
- `DRILL MUTANT APPLIED (1 site) -> D:/projexts/moe-next/tests/migration/cutover/cutover-manifest.ts` printed on both runs.
- ARM C3 RED: `AssertionError: expected { descended: true, declared: false } to deeply equal { descended: false, declared: true }`, `Tests  1 failed | 24 skipped (25)`.

  `Error: CUTOVER_MANIFEST_ENTRY_LIMIT_EXCEEDED @ cutover-manifest: entry count exceeds 10000 (stopped at .moe/tasks/task-e62e3828df234c66969a99b8223487f4.json). ADMITTED POPULATION by top-level segment, largest first: .serena=4303 apps=2884 packages=1763 .moe=1103 tests=277 tools=81 adapters=27 docs=25 .claude=19 scripts=14 .idea=13 .github=11. EXCLUSIONS IN FORCE: .git, dist, node_modules, target. Read the census before touching MAX_WALK_ENTRIES (10000): ...`
  The census reproduces step 1's independent `find|awk` breakdown exactly (4303/2884/1763), and the whole case cost 526 ms. Both arms name the missing exclusion, which is what the drill was for.

RESTORE PROOF, in a call SEPARATE from the drill. Pre-flight `git status --porcelain` on both paths recorded BEFORE anything (` M` both — my own step 2-4 work, no peer edits). Out-of-tree backups taken BEFORE the drill, suffixed by worker id, and grepped to prove pre-mutation vintage (`grep -c '"\.serena",'` = 1 in the backup). After: SHA256 of both live files EQUAL to their backups (manifest 4aa5bbad…c7a3, drill test 1a193d01…10f2), `diff -q` IDENTICAL for both, `grep -n '"\.serena",'` still finds line 143 on disk, and `git status --porcelain -- tests/migration/` shows only those two ` M` entries — no leftover artifact in-tree.   for d in .git .serena dist node_modules target .moe; do git ls-files "$d" | wc -l; done
  .git=0  .serena=972  dist=0  node_modules=0  target=0  .moe=1034

So excluding the name DOES stop manifesting 972 tracked files, and my draft applied a standard to `.moe` that `.serena` also fails. That is exactly the kind of claim a reviewer should have caught rather than me, so I rewrote the comment to disclose it: 972 of 4303 tracked, the other 3331 (77%) host-local session churn; `.moe` is 94% tracked against `.serena`'s 23%, which is the real difference between the two calls.

WHY THE EXCLUSION STILL SHIPS. The walk matches by NAME, not by path prefix (cutover-manifest.ts visitDirent: `limits.excludedNames.has(dirent.name)`). Admitting `.serena/*` while skipping `.serena/memories/*` is NOT EXPRESSIBLE in the current mechanism, so the choice was all-or-nothing against a directory that is 77% host-local churn and 41% of the entire walk. Agent notes ABOUT the repository are not the legacy system being cut over.

FOLLOW-UP, recorded here rather than as a row (DELIVERY BIAS: follow-up items go in a comment on the owning row). If a later row needs those 970 tracked memories manifested, the change is PATH-PREFIX EXCLUSION in the walk — an excluded-prefix set alongside `excludedDirectoryNames`, declared in `excludedDirectories` the same way so `CUTOVER_MANIFEST_EXCLUSION_MISMATCH` keeps failing closed — NOT a bigger `MAX_WALK_ENTRIES`. Nothing on this board currently gates on it, and the walk has 37% headroom without it.

WHY THE EXCLUSION CANNOT HIDE A REAL CUTOVER DIFFERENCE, answered against the module's own contract rather than by assertion: the skipped name is DECLARED in `manifest.excludedDirectories` (ARM C3 asserts the declaration, not merely the absence — absence alone is also what a walk that returned nothing produces), and `compareCutoverManifests` refuses any comparison whose two captures declared different exclusion sets with `CUTOVER_MANIFEST_EXCLUSION_MISMATCH` (pinned by ARM D1). A widened exclusion between two captures fails closed; it cannot masquerade as a match.
